spacr.cli_store:
``spacr store``: check a project's image store from the command line (item 0aj).

``spacr store verify <project>`` (also ``spacr-store verify <project>``)
re-hashes every channel plane of ``<project>/fov.ome.zarr`` against the
sha256 recorded when it was written and, when the original images are still
in the project folder or ``orig/``, compares each stored plane with its
original, value, dtype and shape. It exits 0 only when every plane matches.
spacr.cli_store.build_parser:
Build the ``spacr store`` argument parser.

:returns: the parser, with the ``verify`` subcommand.
spacr.cli_store.main:
Run ``spacr store``.

:param argv: the arguments after ``store``; None reads the process arguments.
:returns: 0 when every plane matches, 1 on any mismatch or error.
:raises SystemExit: status 2 for invalid arguments.
spacr.crop_store.crop_rows:
The crop-index rows of some objects, by key (item 0aj): no table scan.

The lookup goes through spacr.store's key table, which locates the rows
and reads only their row groups, so one crop or a batch of crops costs
the same whatever the project's size.

:param project: the project folder.
:param object_ids: the objects' ``object_id`` keys.
:returns: the rows in the order asked (missing keys left out), or None
    when the project's index is not in the store (an older project; use
    :func:`_read_crop_index`).
spacr.crop_store.crop_to_fov:
Map crop pixel coordinates into the source field's pixel grid (item 0aj).

:param row: the crop's index row (its ``coordinate_transformations``).
:param ys: crop row coordinates.
:param xs: crop column coordinates.
:returns: ``(fov_ys, fov_xs)``: scale, then translation, as 0.6 orders a sequence.
spacr.crop_store.crop_transformations:
Where a crop came from, as OME-Zarr 0.6 coordinate transformations (item 0aj).

A crop's pixel grid (coordinate system ``crop``, axes y, x) maps into
its source field's pixel grid (coordinate system ``fov:<row>/<col>/<field>``
of ``fov.ome.zarr``) by ``scale`` (1, 1 unless the crop was resized)
then a translation to the box's top-left corner (bbox y0, x0, which
already include the margin). Crops sit in pooled arrays, not one
OME-Zarr image each, and 0.6 has no reference from one store's
coordinate system into another store, so the transformation is kept
with each crop's index row (JSON), naming the source store and field
key beside it. :func:`crop_to_fov` applies it.

:returns: the JSON text of ``{"input", "output", "source_store",
    "source_key", "transformations": [scale, translation]}``.
spacr.crop_store.read_crop_labels:
Every object class's labels cut to a crop's box (item 0aj).

:param project: the project folder.
:param row: the crop's table row; ``label_classes`` names the classes.
:returns: ``{class: labels (h, w)}`` in the stored integer dtype; empty
    for a crop of an older project, which stored its own mask only.
    ``labels[row['object_type']] == row['object_label']`` is the crop's
    own-object mask.
spacr.crop_store.read_training_dataset:
The rows of a training dataset saved by :func:`write_training_dataset`.

:param project: the project folder.
:param name: the dataset name.
:returns: every committed row, ready for :func:`read_crop`.
spacr.crop_store.write_training_dataset:
Save a training dataset as its own OME-Zarr crop store (item 0aj).

Each selected crop is read through the one crop reader (stored or
streamed) and written, with every class's labels, through the shared
crop writer into ``<project>/datasets/<name>.ome.zarr``, by plate, well
and object class. Every row keeps the keys back to the measured object
(``source_object_id``, ``plate``, ``well``, ``field``, ``object_type``,
``object_label``) and its ``class`` and ``split``. A dataset written
again under the same name replaces the earlier one.

:param project: the project folder the crops come from.
:param name: the dataset name (the generated dataset folder's name).
:param rows: crop-index rows with ``class`` and ``split`` columns.
:returns: the dataset's rows, pointing at its own pools (their
    ``crop_store`` is relative to ``project``), in the order given.
spacr.image_store.PlateWriter.write_labe:
Add label images to a committed field, never touching its channels (item 0aj P1c).

The field's image arrays are left as they are, so their recorded
checksums still hold; labels of a class not in ``labels`` (left by an
earlier run) are removed. The field is committed again with its
earlier ledger values updated by ``record``.

:param well: the well name.
:param field: the field number.
:param labels: ``{object class: label image (Y, X)}``.
:param record: ledger values to add, such as the merged ``shape``.
:returns: the field's store key.
:raises ValueError: the field has no committed image.
spacr.image_store.original_planes:
The acquired images of a project's fields, plane by plane as fov.ome.zarr keeps them (item 0aj).

The raw images in the project folder and in ``orig/`` are grouped with
the filename pattern of the recorded Mask settings, by the same
function Mask stacking uses, and ordered as the store keeps its
channels (the sorted channel names, then the run's ``channels``).

:param project: the project folder.
:param settings: Mask settings naming ``metadata_type`` and
    ``custom_regex``; by default the ones the project recorded.
:returns: ``({field file name: [loader of each plane]}, notes)``. A
    loader reads its file only when called. A field whose channel was
    projected from several z slices or files has no single original
    plane, so it is left out with a note.
spacr.image_store.verify_project:
``spacr store verify``: the recorded checksums and, when present, the originals (item 0aj).

:param project: the project folder or its ``fov.ome.zarr``.
:param originals: also compare every stored plane with its original
    image, when the originals are in the project folder or ``orig/``.
:returns: :func:`verify_store`'s report plus ``originals_compared``
    (planes compared with an original) and ``notes``.
spacr.image_store.verify_store:
Re-hash every committed field's channel planes against what was recorded (item 0aj).

The channels of ``fov.ome.zarr`` are the acquired pixels, byte for byte;
this is the check every run ends with and that
``keep_original_images=False`` passes before it deletes an original.

:param store: the project's ``fov.ome.zarr`` (or the project folder).
:param originals: optional ``{field file name: [plane, ...]}`` to compare
    the stored planes with as well (value, dtype and shape).
:returns: ``{"fields": n, "planes": n, "mismatches": [...], "unrecorded": [...]}``;
    a field written before hashes were recorded is listed as unrecorded.
